name: Cassino
description: Cassino (also spelled Casino) is a classic fishing-capture card game originating in Italy and popular throughout the world. Players capture cards from a central tableau by matching rank (pairing) or arithmetic sum (combining). Special prizes exist for the Ten of Diamonds ('Big Cassino', worth 2 points) and Two of Spades ('Little Cassino', worth 1 point). The first player or team to reach 11 (or 21 in some variants) points wins.

history.origins: Cassino is one of the oldest fishing-type games in European card culture, with Italian origins. It was described in English-language card game books as early as the late 18th century.
timeline: 1700s: First documented in Italian and French sources as a fishing card game.
1800s: Spread through Europe; documented in English by Hoyle.
1900s: Common in American households; many regional variants develop.
Present: Widely taught as a children's and family game; many national variants (Royal Cassino, Draw Cassino, etc.).
history.cultural: A game taught to children as an introduction to arithmetic and card handling. Remains popular in Scandinavia, the Caribbean, and North America.
history.evolution: The building mechanicâ€”combining table cards into a 'build' that can only be taken with the matching rankâ€”is Cassino's most sophisticated feature, unique among fishing games.

setup.dealing: 4 cards each; 4 cards face-up on table (the 'tableau'). Rest is stock. Redeal 4 each when hands empty until stock gone.

rules.objective: Score 11 points (or 21) before opponents. Points come from special cards, counting cards, and spades.
rules.gameplay:
On your turn, play exactly one card from your hand by:
1. Pairing: If your card matches a table card's rank, capture both.
2. Combining: If your card equals the arithmetic sum of 2+ table cards, capture them all.
3. Building: Lay your hand card with table cards, announce the intended total. Another player cannot steal the build unless they match it first.
4. Trailing: If you can't or won't capture/build, simply lay a card face-up on the table.
keyRules: Face cards (J, Q, K) have no numeric value for combining; they can only pair.
A 'sweep' (clearing entire tableau) earns 1 bonus point. The sweeping card is turned face-up to track sweeps.
All table cards not captured go to the last player who made any capture.

strategy.basic: Always capture Big Cassino (10â™¦) and Little Cassino (2â™ ) when possibleâ€”combined they're 3 points. Never let them sit on the table unguarded.
strategy.intermediate: Build Management: Build toward a number you hold in your hand. Don't announce a build unless you're confident no opponent holds the matching capture card. Monitor the count of cards you've capturedâ€”crossing 27 cards triggers the Most Cards bonus (3 pts).
strategy.advanced: Sweep Timing: Set up a sweep (clearing the table) within 2-3 turns by building so all table cards combine into your target number. Track all four Acesâ€”each is a point. In 2-player, count the spades gone to predict whether you or your opponent will hit the 7-spade threshold.
tips: Never trail a card that creates an easy capture opportunity for your opponent.
Keep track of cards captured throughout the hand, not just at scoring.
In partnership play, coordinate to deny opponents Big/Little Cassino.

variations.name: Royal Cassino
variations.description: Aces count as 1 OR 14. Jacks = 11, Queens = 12, Kings = 13 for building purposes. Creates much richer building combinations.

variations.name: Draw Cassino
variations.description: Players draw to replenish hand to 4 after each turn, rather than waiting for the whole hand to run out.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant changes draw timing; engine overrides to be added when implemented.

scoring.description: Point awards for special cards, most cards, most spades, and sweeps.
